newsitem.title: USA: Oklahoma wheat planting, corn harvesting resume.
newsitem.headline: Oklahoma wheat planting, corn harvesting resume.

text.p: Relatively dry weather enabled Okalahoma farmers to resume winter wheat planting and row crop harvesting during the week ended Sunday, according to the state's Agricultural Statistics Service.
"Wet fields kept producers out of the fields early in the week, but by mid-week many acres were dry enough to prepare seedbeds and begin planting," the report said.
The report also noted that army worm infestation was heavy in some areas where the wheat crop was emerging.
Wheat planting advanced to 46 percent, versus last-year's pace of 36 percent and the five-year average of 64 percent.
Corn harvested 75 percent vs 60 y/a, 84 average.
Corn mature 85 percent vs 87 y/a, 97 avge.
Sorghum harvested 15 percent vs 6 y/a, 13 avge.
Sorghum mature 45 percent vs 19 y/a, 40 avge.
Soybeans harvested 23 percent vs 22 y/a, 21 avge.
Soybeans mature 74 pct vs 50 y/a, 58 avge.
Soybeans rated 71 pct good to excellent, 23 fair, 6 poor.
Cotton bolls opening 59 percent vs 20 y/a, 53 avge.
Cotton harvested 1 percent vs nil y/a, 8 avge.
Pasture and range condition was rated 79 pct good to excellent.
